original_value: Stripe noise removal continues to be an active field of research for remote image processing. Most existing approaches are prone to generating artifacts in extreme areas and removing the stripe-like details. In this paper, a weighted double sparsity unidirectional variation (WDSUV) model is constructed to reduce this phenomenon. The WDSUV takes advantage of both the spatial domain and the gradient domain’s sparse property of stripe noise, and processes the heavy stripe area, extreme area and regular noise corrupted areas using different strategies. The proposed model consists of two variation terms and two sparsity terms that can well exploit the intrinsic properties of stripe noise. Then, the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) optimal solver is employed to solve the optimization model in an alternating minimization scheme. Compared with the state-of-the-art approaches, the experimental results on both the synthetic and real remote sensing data demonstrate that the proposed model has a better destriping performance in terms of the preservation of small details, stripe noise estimation and in the mean time for artifacts’ reduction.

result.paraphrase: Stripe noise removal remains an active research topic in remote image processing. Most existing methods tend to introduce artifacts in extreme regions and erase stripe-like details. To mitigate this issue, this paper develops a weighted double sparsity unidirectional variation (WDSUV) model. WDSUV exploits the sparse characteristics of stripe noise in both the spatial and gradient domains, and applies different strategies to heavy stripe regions, extreme areas, and regular noise-contaminated regions. The proposed model includes two variation terms and two sparsity terms, which effectively leverage the intrinsic properties of stripe noise. An alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) optimizer is then used to solve the optimization model via an alternating minimization scheme. Experimental results on both synthetic and real remote sensing data show that, compared with state-of-the-art methods, the proposed model achieves better destriping performance by preserving small details, improving stripe noise estimation, and reducing artifacts.
